newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angola willing to help end Zaire crisis - U.N. envoy.
newsitem.headline: Angola willing to help end Zaire crisis - U.N. envoy.

text.p: Angolan President Jose Eduardo dos Santos is totally willing to help resolve the crisis in his northern neighbour Zaire, a U.N. special envoy trying to end the conflict said on Wednesday.
Mohamed Sahnoun, who represents the United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity in his efforts to find peace in Zaire, said dos Santos had offered to help where he could.
"President dos Santos has expressed his total willingness to make a contribution in finding a solution to the Zaire crisis," Sahnoun told reporters after talks on Wednesday afternoon.
The U.N. representative, accompanied by an aide, met the president and Angolan Foreign Minister Venancio de Moura for 30 minutes before 10 minutes of private talks with dos Santos.
Western diplomats in Luanda earlier said Angolan government soldiers were backing Laurent Kabila's rebel forces in their fight against Zaire President Mobutu Sese Seko.

The Zairean president is a long-time ally of Angola's UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi and his country held many of its supply bases and logistics channels during the two decades it fought the Angolan government.
Asked if he had discussed the Angolan government's reported military support for Kabila, Sahnoun said: "All I can say is that we discussed all the aspects of the Zairean conflict."

An African diplomat in Luanda said Sahnoun's visit to Luanda was part of diplomacy aimed at arranging a direct meeting between Kabila and Mobutu. Kabila has taken more than half of Zaire since going to war against Mobutu's forces last October.

The rebel leader has proposed talks with Mobutu in Lubumbashi, Zaire's second city that his rebels hold. Kabila has rejected a proposal from President Pascal Lissouba of Congo that the talks take place in his capital, Brazzaville -- across the river from Kinshasa.
